name: VideoWhisper Agentic Multilingual Translator
author: videowhisper

sections.description:
Create language versions of public, unprotected Posts and Pages while keeping the original intact. Translate manually in WordPress or use your own connected AI assistant to prepare drafts. Local editing needs no translation-service account, model subscription or API key from this plugin.

Included features:

  • Review queue for missing/stale pages and supported plugin/user texts, protected corrections and publication readiness.

  • Opt-in registered text adapters, approved comment overlays, site labels and existing plugin MO catalogs on resolved language pages. Drafts and notes stay private until separate publication.

  • Resumable private translation plans for longer pages, with small batches, retry receipts, native progress review and one complete draft at the end. Partial work never changes a public translation.

  • Native paginated source/translation comparisons and explicitly reviewed section protection. Uncertain or moved WPBakery sections fall back to whole-field protection.
  • Private localized Post/Page URL proposals, separately published paths and retained local redirect aliases. In-body and supported reusable Navigation links follow available published variants.
  • Local title, excerpt, content, search title and meta-description translations, private drafts, revisions and source-freshness checks.
  • Explicit stale-translation refresh plans that reuse verified unchanged units and retain protected manual corrections. Native editors control field protection; assistants cannot unlock it.
  • Brief private progress/review notes per translation, plus source editorial notes from Site Manager when installed. Notes accompany authenticated context/review and remain outside public pages and indexes.
  • Published locale-prefixed URLs such as /fr/about/, canonical/hreflang support and a server-rendered language selector.
  • Configurable missing-translation behavior.
  • Bounded plain-text extraction for supported static core blocks, Classic HTML and common WPBakery text, buttons, headings, call-to-action and pricing-card labels. Builder structure, links, code and non-text attributes stay preserved. Unknown or dynamic elements require manual editing.
  • Versioned Free PHP API and public actions/filters for other AI plugins. Optional Site Manager tools let users translate their own public content in enabled site languages, save drafts and publish only when configured permissions allow.
  • Separate native integration and publication opt-ins, both off by default. WordPress capabilities, author ownership, source/target versions, extraction inventory and context expiry remain checked.
  • Existing optional native WordPress Abilities continue to read permitted originals and save private drafts only; no publication ability is exposed.
  • Shared Free models and rendering hooks for localized public terms and classic navigation overlays, with separately authorized administration supplied by an integration.
  • Data retention by default. Retiring a language keeps its existing public translations and stops new translation work.

Start in Multilingual Translator > Onboarding, choose languages and use Translation editor. Review meaning, links and layout before publication. Provider connection-test screens do not perform automatic page translation. The admin interface currently uses English fallback; no bundled interface locales are provided yet.

Requires WordPress 6.9+ and PHP 8.2+. Prefer a currently maintained newer PHP branch.

Translated SEO and safe refresh

Search titles and meta descriptions share the translation draft, revision and publication lifecycle. Native limits are 250 and 500 characters. Blank SEO fields use the published translated title or excerpt. Supported output owners are WordPress core, Agentic Optimization standalone, Site Manager standalone, Yoast SEO, Rank Math and SEOPress. Only the existing owner emits its description. Unknown or competing owners require native integration review. Source provider templates fall back to original title/excerpt text instead of executing or publishing template syntax. Trusted integrations may supply resolved source text through vwml_translation_seo_source_v1. Source SEO settings and owner changes participate in freshness. This is title/description support, not translation of arbitrary schema, social cards, robots policies or provider metadata. Localized URL proposals are reviewed separately as described below.

Choose Refresh an existing translation in Translation plans, or use the separately reviewed Site Manager refresh-plan tool. Verified unchanged units are reused; repeated text with ambiguous identity is translated again after inventory changes. New or changed text arrives in ordinary resumable batches. A complete refresh saves one private draft and receipt. The live page remains unchanged until separately authorized publication.

Manual changes protect the entire edited field, including its builder markup. Older translations without a saved baseline default to protected nonempty fields. The native editor lists protection choices: uncheck an unchanged field and save only after reviewing whether it may be replaced. Agents cannot remove protection. Protected fields remain intact even when the source changes and are explicitly returned for review. A source, SEO owner, target, protection or permission change during work requires a new plan. Existing translations, notes, permissions and revision history are retained on upgrade. Earlier source hashes may conservatively appear stale after the new SEO-aware fingerprint is introduced.

Reviewed sections, URLs and navigation

Open Source changes and translation review in the native editor to compare the previous/current source with the saved translation. After correcting a field, choose the sections to protect and explicitly save that native review. Section approval requires the unchanged source inventory and a target that round-trips through source-owned markup. Other edits, moved/repeated units or uncertain structure keep the complete field protected. Assistants can read differences, but cannot remove protection. A later native field edit restores whole-field protection until reviewed again.

Language URL proposals stay private until translation publication. Publication applies the reviewed local path, keeps earlier published paths as direct local aliases and fails without partial changes on collision, stale source or unsupported transactional storage. A maximum of 20 paths is retained per original/language. Default paths are bound on publication; existing older variants acquire that record on their next publication. No remote redirect destinations are accepted. Original permalink edits do not silently replace a bound language URL.

Links in public content and supported core Navigation output resolve available published Post/Page variants, preserving ordinary query data and fragments. External, preview/authentication, pagination and missing-translation links retain their destination. Reusable published Navigation menus support bounded plain label overlays for static links/submenus; dynamic, fallback and split rich labels remain unchanged. Separate administrative integration tools require menu permissions. Translated labels never change the original link inventory or block structure.

Local extensions can supply bounded advisory guidance through vwml_translation_guidance_v1 and recheck frozen plan guidance through vwml_translation_guidance_read_v1. Guidance never grants tools, changes units or publishes. Plans retain captured guidance; extensions can withhold advice that becomes stale without erasing progress.

Resumable translation plans

Enable integration access in Translator Settings, add target languages, then open Translation plans or the resumable-batches link in an owned original’s translation editor. Native controls can save batches; connected assistants use Site Manager’s separately reviewed translation_plan_* tools. A plan ID identifies private work and is never a credential. The creating WordPress user must retain the required source capabilities, ownership or separate administrative authority, current site/connection/personal approvals and enabled language.

Create a plan with a stable request key, read its next missing batch, translate exactly the returned plain-text units and submit each complete batch with its own stable key. Identical retries return the prior receipt; changed payloads conflict. After reconnecting, read status rather than starting duplicate work. Completion uses the latest plan version and creates one private draft and durable receipt in the same transaction. Review that draft in the normal editor; publication remains a separate authorized operation.

Plans allow 256 KiB original source, 1024 text units, 8 KiB per unit and 1 MiB assembled draft. Batches contain at most 8 units and 16 KiB of original text. Plans expire after seven days, with 20 active and 100 retained plans per user and 1000 per site. Plan operations require InnoDB storage for the plugin’s plan/translation tables and WordPress posts/postmeta tables, so the complete-draft transaction can also protect its source snapshot. Source, target, adapter, implementation or native policy changes require a fresh plan. Existing short-context/native Ability limits remain unchanged.

Cancelled and expired work stays private until deliberately removed. Delete plan progress only when its receipt and staged batches are no longer needed; saved translations, original content and notes remain. Default uninstall retains data. Site administrators can maintain closed progress without gaining the ability to resume another user’s batches. Supported static builder elements preserve layout, URLs, amounts and non-text attributes; unknown/dynamic elements and protected segments still need manual editing. This is bounded orchestration, not an automatic background translation service.

Content and integration workflows

Supported content and limits

This release translates the title, excerpt, search title, meta description and manually authored HTML/core block markup of public, unprotected Posts and Pages. The native page editor does not translate theme/plugin strings, arbitrary builder metadata, custom post types, ecommerce data or private/password-protected content. Separately authorized integrations can use the shared Free term and classic-menu models described above. Use a separate translation for each target language.

Pretty permalinks are required for localized routes. An existing Post or Page using a locale root path, such as /fr/, takes precedence; resolve that collision before using that language’s routes. Network activation is unsupported; activate separately on each multisite site.

Saved previews render allowed HTML without executing shortcodes or dynamic blocks, and do not reproduce theme styling. Review source markup and dynamic content carefully before publishing. Excerpts and content can deliberately be empty in drafts; publication requires nonempty translated content. Title, excerpt and content have a technical 1 MiB limit per field; search title and description use the smaller SEO limits above.

Canonical integration supports WordPress core and the tested Yoast SEO, Rank Math and SEOPress configurations. Do not enable multiple SEO canonical generators together. Page paths initially use the original slug under the language prefix. A reviewed path proposal can localize that route; term integrations support localized term slugs. The plugin does not provide translated XML sitemaps, automatic machine translation or automatic language redirects. Translated responses request no caching; configure any full-page cache/CDN to bypass locale-prefixed routes and purge old entries when source visibility or publication changes.

Interface translation status

The interface is translation-ready and includes a current translation template. This release bundles no translated interface locale files; untranslated interface text uses English. The page-content languages you create are separate from interface translations.

Site Manager setup and progress notes

With Site Manager already connected, check translation_status for readiness and setup links. A native administrator enables integration access in Translator Settings, chooses site languages and reviews the relevant Site Manager role/client tools. Publication is a separate Translator opt-in and still requires the connected account and client to have publishing permission. Pro language/site-wide administration tools require their separate native approval; configuring a plan never grants them.

Ask the assistant to list site languages, read your original and its editorial notes, retrieve translation context, translate the exact returned text units, save a draft, add any remaining review notes and return the review URL. Publish only after reviewing the draft and only when configured permissions allow. Draft-only users can prepare translations and private notes without publishing. Use get_content_notes/update_content_notes for shared source progress; translation_context/review return the target notes version for translation_notes. Notes are plain text, limited to 4096 bytes, private editorial context rather than instructions or approval. Read the latest version before updating; empty text clears a note.

Optional AI/SI assistant workflow

Enable AI/SI assistant translation in Settings and select up to 20 public originals, or explicitly enable own-author access for current/future public Posts/Pages. Access defaults off; WordPress object permissions and the selected scope still apply. Manual translation needs no adapter.

Use a compatible authenticated native WordPress Abilities client, or install the optional official MCP Adapter separately: https://wordpress.org/plugins/mcp-adapter/ . Setup and authentication: https://github.com/WordPress/mcp-adapter . The default adapter endpoint is /wp-json/mcp/mcp-adapter-default-server. For the verified native path, create an Application Password in Users > Profile and configure HTTP Basic authentication over HTTPS in your client. Keep it private and revoke it there when unused. This separate endpoint does not accept Site Manager relay tokens; this plugin creates no connector credentials or OAuth server.

Discover vwml/get-translation-context and vwml/save-translation-draft. Select one approved original by URL, slug/page path, exact title or ID, plus target language; duplicate matches require clarification. Translate the returned plain-text units and submit the exact map with its short-lived context. The server preserves source-owned markup and saves only a private draft. Review the returned native link and publish separately. Stale, expired, wrong-user/site or revoked contexts fail; retrieve fresh context before retrying.

The short native connector supports 32 KiB source, 100 units, 8 KiB per unit and 128 KiB assembled draft. Resumable plan limits are separate. Unsupported/dynamic content, placeholders, code and protected segments require manual review. No text is silently truncated. There is no provider Translate button, scheduled translation job or publication Ability.

Privacy

The plugin stores configured languages, translation drafts/public snapshots, revisions with editor IDs/timestamps, private plan batches and bounded extension advice, review provenance, local route aliases and a bounded administration activity history. It makes no external service requests, records no visitor metrics, and sets no tracking cookies. Optional AI/SI assistants can request allowed source text only after administrator opt-in and WordPress authorization; their processing is covered by their own service policies. Export is administrator-only and checks edit permission on each source; credentials and visitor data are excluded.

If upgrading an earlier development build, existing provider credentials and legacy operational tables are retained but unused. They are never contacted or included in translation exports. The explicitly confirmed uninstall deletion option removes both current and legacy plugin data. Keep sensitive server configuration outside the plugin folder.

External services

The plugin makes no external service requests itself. The optional official MCP Adapter operates on your WordPress site and is documented at https://github.com/WordPress/mcp-adapter . When you request translation through a connected assistant, allowed original text is returned to that client; its configured AI provider may process the text and charge for it. The client/provider is chosen and configured by you, not selected or contacted by this plugin. Review that service’s processing, privacy policy, terms and costs before connecting; disabling access stops subsequent translator ability calls. The plugin does not collect or store their keys, register an account, send telemetry or share visitor data.

Developer integration contract

The Free plugin owns the local data and rendering contracts. VWML_API::VERSION is 1. Use its languages, inventory, context, save, review, publish and public_variant methods from an independently authenticated, capability-checked integration. Own-source access and publication are separate native settings, both off by default. Never treat the signed context as authentication: it is also bound to current WordPress user/site, source and target revisions, settings, extraction inventory and expiry. The older native abilities remain draft-only. Contexts issued before an implementation/inventory change must be reread.

Extension hooks include vwml_loaded, vwml_translation_source_fields, vwml_wpbakery_label_attributes, vwml_translation_units_prepared, vwml_integration_draft_saved, vwml_translation_published, vwml_translation_saved, vwml_language_state_changed, vwml_languages_changed, vwml_element_saved, vwml_use_public_overlay and vwml_route_url. Filters are trusted PHP extension points, not client-controlled arguments. Source fields must remain exactly title/excerpt/content strings within the safe extraction bounds. Lifecycle events expose identifiers and counts, not credentials or signed contexts. The vwml_integration_administration filter lets a trusted companion provide administration; native manage_options and applicable object capabilities remain mandatory.
sections.installation:
Upgrading from the previous development name: deactivate the previous VideoWhisper translator, install/activate this plugin and retain the database. Both identities share translation data; do not enable uninstall deletion or uninstall the old copy to migrate. Public locale URLs, shortcode and vwml ability names are unchanged. Discovery REST routes now use /wp-json/videowhisper-agentic-multilingual-translator/v1/.

  1. Upload the ZIP through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, or copy the plugin folder into wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate VideoWhisper Agentic Multilingual Translator on the intended site.
  3. Open Agentic Translator > Settings. Confirm the source language, select targets and save. Configure a pretty permalink structure if needed.
  4. Open a public Post or Page and use its Multilingual translations panel, or select its title and target in Agentic Translator > Translation editor.
  5. Enter translated fields, Save draft and review the private preview. Publish translation when ready.
  6. Add [vwml_language_selector] to the source content or a Shortcode widget. It displays published languages only.
  7. Before removing data, download a JSON export from Settings and keep a database backup for complete revision history.
sections.faq:
Can other plugins translate configured messages, bios, comments or reviews?

Yes. Enable a registered public provider in Multilingual Translator > Plugin texts. Adapters re-read source fields and verify ownership/operation permissions; unknown/private fields and caller-supplied ownership are excluded. Native corrections are protected by default. Site Manager Free manages own texts; separately reviewed Pro tools administer site-wide texts. Capture does not approve tools.

Selected PHP plugin domains can use installed MO catalogs, including context/plurals, without changing global/user locale. PO/POT remain editable/source formats; compile MO normally. JavaScript catalogs need their owning plugin’s support. Observed singular strings can have local reviewed overrides. Capture is bounded to 50 new/changed texts per request and 5,000 source identities per site. Changed snippet sources fall back to originals while saved translations/corrections remain available. See the public adapter contract and examples.

WordPress privacy tools handle registered users’ currently supported own overlays. Unavailable, reassigned or guest sources require administrator review; original content and other users remain.

Does it automatically translate my site?

Manual translation always works without another plugin. Optionally enable WordPress Abilities so your connected AI/SI assistant can translate selected text into drafts. This is an explicit assistant workflow, not automatic background translation. The plugin itself does not call translation providers.

Where do translations live?

In custom tables in this site’s WordPress database. Disconnecting accounts has no effect because none are required. JSON export contains the current snapshot and latest draft; a full database backup preserves every historical revision.

What happens when I change the original?

The existing translation is retained and marked stale. A form opened before a source or target change is rejected rather than overwriting newer work. Use the browser Back button to copy unsaved edits, then reload and review the current version.

Can I remove a public translation without deleting it?

Yes. Open it in the translation editor and choose Unpublish. Its content and revisions remain available, and its public link disappears. Deselecting a target language alone retains its existing published pages and stops new edits.

Can I translate protected content?

No. A source becoming private, draft, trashed or password-protected immediately becomes ineligible for translation overlays and public variant discovery. External caches must also be purged.

Which shortcodes and APIs are included?

[vwml_language_selector] and [videowhisper_language_selector] show the current page’s published versions. Use post_id=”123″ outside a singular page. The public read-only REST namespace is videowhisper-agentic-multilingual-translator/v1, with /languages and /variants/{post_id}. Operational /status is administrator-only. When an administrator opts in on a supported WordPress version, native abilities vwml/get-translation-context and vwml/save-translation-draft are available to authenticated clients. An optional MCP Adapter can expose the same abilities; this plugin adds no separate MCP endpoint. No publication ability is exposed.
sections.changelog:
0.10.0

  • Add a permission-checked review queue for missing/stale content, unresolved protection and publication readiness.
  • Add opt-in plugin text adapters, approved comment overlays, site labels, private drafts/notes and separate publication.
  • Read installed plugin MO catalogs on resolved language pages without changing global/user locale; retain source context and plural rules.
  • Preserve native manual corrections, original markup/placeholders and existing permissions; integrate registered-user privacy export/erasure.

0.9.0

  • Added native source differences and reviewed section protection, conservative WPBakery refresh, private localized URL proposals and published aliases.
  • Accept browser form line endings during section review without changing saved corrections, version checks or the conservative fallback for markup changes.
  • Added published Post/Page link resolution, reusable Navigation label contracts and bounded advisory extension/plan hooks.
  • Retained ownership, publication, native review, existing data and exact connection permission boundaries.

0.8.0

  • Add translated search titles and meta descriptions to private drafts, native review and supported single-owner frontend output. Original SEO, noindex and publication controls remain authoritative.
  • Add conservative refresh plans that reuse verified unchanged units, protect manual/legacy fields, retain public snapshots and reject stale source, target or permission changes.
  • Keep manual protection under native editorial control; expose Free hooks and explicit refresh summaries for integrations.

0.7.0

  • Add actor/site/version-bound resumable translation plans, private bounded batches, exact retries, cancellation, expiry and explicit retained-progress cleanup.
  • Atomically save the complete private draft and its durable receipt; retain existing public snapshots until separately authorized publication.
  • Add native progress/batch review, setup links and documented integration hooks. Extend reviewed WPBakery CTA/pricing labels and accept safe inline-style serialization spacing while rejecting KSES-changing markup.
  • Keep existing short-context/native Ability bounds and permissions, default data retention and English fallback.

0.6.1

  • Register localized taxonomy routes after ordinary taxonomy setup and before broad language routes, then refresh cached rules on upgrade.
  • Remove owned taxonomy routes when refreshing languages or deactivating the plugin while retaining customer translations.

0.6.0

  • Private source and per-translation progress notes with versioned updates and authenticated retrieval.
  • Language inventory includes the supported catalog; Romanian is available as an opt-in target.
  • Public query integrations can select published language variants before pagination.
  • Defer language-route registration and flushing until WordPress rewrite services are ready during a fresh installation or early bootstrap.

0.5.0

  • Permission-controlled integration API and hooks; WPBakery text/label preservation; shared term/menu translation model.

0.4.4

  • Escape translated title and document-title output; explicitly filter allowed HTML in content and excerpt callbacks.
  • Limit the previous-plugin conflict notice to authorized users on the Plugins screen, remove an unused onboarding-notice hook, and require POST for legacy dismissal.
  • Require WordPress 6.9+ and PHP 8.2+. Existing translations and settings are retained.

0.4.3

  • Respect WordPress query filters when resolving originals for connected assistants.

0.4.2

  • Assistants can identify an approved original by its same-site URL, slug/page path, exact title or ID. Ambiguous matches require clarification. Access controls and human publication remain unchanged.

0.4.1

  • Rename to VideoWhisper Agentic Multilingual Translator with a matching directory identity and text domain.
  • Retain translations, settings, shortcode and vwml abilities. Prevent simultaneous activation with the previous development identity.

0.4.0

  • Searchable original picker, optional connected-author access, translation review list, Posts/Pages shortcuts and language statuses.
  • Copyable AI/SI assistant prompts; manual review and publication remain required.

0.3.2

  • Explain the verified native MCP authentication flow using Users > Profile > Application Passwords and HTTPS Basic authentication.
  • Link directly to Profile and clarify private credential storage, revocation and separate client connection.

0.3.1

  • Link connector setup to the WordPress.org MCP Adapter installer and identify the correct plugin/author.
  • Show adapter installation/activation status and distinguish installation from client authentication.

0.3.0

  • Add optional native WordPress Abilities and official MCP Adapter discovery for authenticated AI/SI assistant draft translation.
  • Restrict access to explicitly selected public originals and enabled targets, with actor/site/version/expiry/consent checks.
  • Extract bounded plain-text units and assemble source-owned markup; preserve code, placeholders and attributes.
  • Keep manual translation and human-only publication, with connector setup, privacy guidance and review prompts.

0.2.1

  • Select recent originals by title, with an older-source ID option and clear empty states.
  • Add action confirmations, plain-language publication status and original-page shortcuts.
  • Clarify revision recovery and preview direction, and improve small-screen editor layout.

0.2.0

  • Complete manual-first publishing workflow with draft preview, unpublish, recent revision recovery and JSON export.
  • Reject stale source/translation saves and preserve live content when editing drafts.
  • Add reciprocal language links and supported SEO canonical integration; restrict public routes and discovery to eligible published sources.
  • Remove incomplete provider tests and visitor-demand collection from runtime.
  • Retain existing translation data and legacy configuration on upgrade.

0.1.2

  • Preserve source password protection in overlays and public variant discovery.

0.1.1

  • Add target-language defaults and onboarding navigation.

0.1.0

  • Initial local development version.

The native page editor does not translate theme/plugin strings, arbitrary builder metadata, custom post types, ecommerce data or private/password-protected content. Separately authorized integrations can use the shared Free term and classic-menu models described above. Use a separate translation for each target language.

Pretty permalinks are required for localized routes. An existing Post or Page using a locale root path, such as /fr/, takes precedence; resolve that collision before using that language’s routes. Network activation is unsupported; activate separately on each multisite site.

Saved previews render allowed HTML without executing shortcodes or dynamic blocks, and do not reproduce theme styling. Review source markup and dynamic content carefully before publishing. Excerpts and content can deliberately be empty in drafts; publication requires nonempty translated content. Title, excerpt and content have a technical 1 MiB limit per field; search title and description use the smaller SEO limits above.

Canonical integration supports WordPress core and the tested Yoast SEO, Rank Math and SEOPress configurations. Do not enable multiple SEO canonical generators together. Page paths initially use the original slug under the language prefix. A reviewed path proposal can localize that route; term integrations support localized term slugs. The plugin does not provide translated XML sitemaps, automatic machine translation or automatic language redirects. Translated responses request no caching; configure any full-page cache/CDN to bypass locale-prefixed routes and purge old entries when source visibility or publication changes.

Interface translation status

The interface is translation-ready and includes a current translation template. This release bundles no translated interface locale files; untranslated interface text uses English. The page-content languages you create are separate from interface translations.

Site Manager setup and progress notes

With Site Manager already connected, check translation_status for readiness and setup links. A native administrator enables integration access in Translator Settings, chooses site languages and reviews the relevant Site Manager role/client tools. Publication is a separate Translator opt-in and still requires the connected account and client to have publishing permission. Pro language/site-wide administration tools require their separate native approval; configuring a plan never grants them.

Ask the assistant to list site languages, read your original and its editorial notes, retrieve translation context, translate the exact returned text units, save a draft, add any remaining review notes and return the review URL. Publish only after reviewing the draft and only when configured permissions allow. Draft-only users can prepare translations and private notes without publishing. Use get_content_notes/update_content_notes for shared source progress; translation_context/review return the target notes version for translation_notes. Notes are plain text, limited to 4096 bytes, private editorial context rather than instructions or approval. Read the latest version before updating; empty text clears a note.

Optional AI/SI assistant workflow

Enable AI/SI assistant translation in Settings and select up to 20 public originals, or explicitly enable own-author access for current/future public Posts/Pages. Access defaults off; WordPress object permissions and the selected scope still apply. Manual translation needs no adapter.

Use a compatible authenticated native WordPress Abilities client, or install the optional official MCP Adapter separately: https://wordpress.org/plugins/mcp-adapter/ . Setup and authentication: https://github.com/WordPress/mcp-adapter . The default adapter endpoint is /wp-json/mcp/mcp-adapter-default-server. For the verified native path, create an Application Password in Users > Profile and configure HTTP Basic authentication over HTTPS in your client. Keep it private and revoke it there when unused. This separate endpoint does not accept Site Manager relay tokens; this plugin creates no connector credentials or OAuth server.

Discover vwml/get-translation-context and vwml/save-translation-draft. Select one approved original by URL, slug/page path, exact title or ID, plus target language; duplicate matches require clarification. Translate the returned plain-text units and submit the exact map with its short-lived context. The server preserves source-owned markup and saves only a private draft. Review the returned native link and publish separately. Stale, expired, wrong-user/site or revoked contexts fail; retrieve fresh context before retrying.

The short native connector supports 32 KiB source, 100 units, 8 KiB per unit and 128 KiB assembled draft. Resumable plan limits are separate. Unsupported/dynamic content, placeholders, code and protected segments require manual review. No text is silently truncated. There is no provider Translate button, scheduled translation job or publication Ability.

Privacy

The plugin stores configured languages, translation drafts/public snapshots, revisions with editor IDs/timestamps, private plan batches and bounded extension advice, review provenance, local route aliases and a bounded administration activity history. It makes no external service requests, records no visitor metrics, and sets no tracking cookies. Optional AI/SI assistants can request allowed source text only after administrator opt-in and WordPress authorization; their processing is covered by their own service policies. Export is administrator-only and checks edit permission on each source; credentials and visitor data are excluded.

If upgrading an earlier development build, existing provider credentials and legacy operational tables are retained but unused. They are never contacted or included in translation exports. The explicitly confirmed uninstall deletion option removes both current and legacy plugin data. Keep sensitive server configuration outside the plugin folder.

External services

The plugin makes no external service requests itself. The optional official MCP Adapter operates on your WordPress site and is documented at https://github.com/WordPress/mcp-adapter . When you request translation through a connected assistant, allowed original text is returned to that client; its configured AI provider may process the text and charge for it. The client/provider is chosen and configured by you, not selected or contacted by this plugin. Review that service’s processing, privacy policy, terms and costs before connecting; disabling access stops subsequent translator ability calls. The plugin does not collect or store their keys, register an account, send telemetry or share visitor data.

Developer integration contract

The Free plugin owns the local data and rendering contracts. VWML_API::VERSION is 1. Use its languages, inventory, context, save, review, publish and public_variant methods from an independently authenticated, capability-checked integration. Own-source access and publication are separate native settings, both off by default. Never treat the signed context as authentication: it is also bound to current WordPress user/site, source and target revisions, settings, extraction inventory and expiry. The older native abilities remain draft-only. Contexts issued before an implementation/inventory change must be reread.

Extension hooks include vwml_loaded, vwml_translation_source_fields, vwml_wpbakery_label_attributes, vwml_translation_units_prepared, vwml_integration_draft_saved, vwml_translation_published, vwml_translation_saved, vwml_language_state_changed, vwml_languages_changed, vwml_element_saved, vwml_use_public_overlay and vwml_route_url. Filters are trusted PHP extension points, not client-controlled arguments. Source fields must remain exactly title/excerpt/content strings within the safe extraction bounds. Lifecycle events expose identifiers and counts, not credentials or signed contexts. The vwml_integration_administration filter lets a trusted companion provide administration; native manage_options and applicable object capabilities remain mandatory.
